summary: Appends a node to the tail of a doubly linked list. Head pointer lives at this+0x1518 (this[1350]); node links are prev at node+0x1C and next at node+0x20. If the list is non-empty it walks from the head to the tail via next pointers, then sets a2's prev (+0x1C) to the old tail and the old tail's next (+0x20) to a2. If the list is empty it sets the head to a2. Returns a2 in all paths.

operations.description: Read head pointer this[1350] at offset 0x1518; if null the list is empty and the new node becomes the head.
Walk from the head following next pointers at node+0x20 until the tail (node whose next is null) is reached.
Non-empty path: set a2's prev (+0x1C) to the old tail and set the old tail's next (+0x20) to a2.
Empty path: set head this[1350] (offset 0x1518) to a2.
Return a2 (the appended node) in all paths.

unresolved: Unlike a fully initializing append, a2's next (+0x20) is never explicitly zeroed here and the empty path does not initialize a2's links; the caller is expected to have pre-initialized the new node.

The packet field base *(*(this+0x1538)+0x20) is the existing analysis's interpretation of the next-pointer location; raw source accesses this[1350] and node+0x20 directly, and 0x1538 is not read in the raw source.
